cultivar: Clonal bushes with large buds (AV2 and local selections)
processing: Bud-heavy pluckings fully oxidised in the orthodox way and only lightly rolled so the buds stay intact; the down turns golden-orange and dominates the sorted grade.
harvest_season: Second flush (May–June) and autumn (October–November), when the buds are fattest.
appearance_dry: Golden-orange downy buds with a little dark leaf.
taste_profile: Sweet, honeyed malt with cocoa and dried apricot, a thick, soft body and very little astringency.

brewing.notes: No milk needed; hard to over-brew, and a second steep is as good as the first.

vintage_note: Sold as a top grade by season and year from named factories under names such as 'Golden Tips', 'Golden Buds' or 'Himalayan Golden', with summer lots from July and autumn lots from November. Keeps two to three years sealed; many drinkers find it rounder after a few months' rest.
description:
Golden tips from Nepal are the bud-heavy black teas of the eastern hills: pluckings rich in fat, downy buds, fully oxidised so that the down turns golden-orange, and sorted so the buds dominate. They are the showpiece grade of many Ilam and Dhankuta factories, and in a good year they rival the golden-tip Assams and Yunnan's dian hong for sweetness while keeping a lighter, Himalayan touch.

The leaf is made the orthodox way: withered, lightly rolled to keep the buds intact, fully oxidised and gently fired. Buds carry little tannin and plenty of sugars and aromatic compounds, so the cup is soft and sweet rather than brisk. The best lots come from the second flush in late spring and from autumn, when the buds are fattest.

Expect a bright copper-gold cup with honeyed malt, cocoa and dried apricot, a thick, soft body and very little astringency. Brew it at about 90 °C for three to four minutes without milk and give it a second steep; it is hard to over-brew.

It is sold as a top grade by season and year from named factories under names such as 'Golden Tips', 'Golden Buds' or 'Himalayan Golden', with summer lots from July and autumn lots from November. It keeps two or three years sealed, and many drinkers find it rounder after a few months' rest.

A good one for people who think they do not like black tea: there is almost no bitterness to find.
history:
Golden tips is a style and a grade rather than the product of any one garden, and little is documented about when Nepalese factories started making it. Tea in eastern Nepal grew from the Ilam plantation of the 1860s, but the country's orthodox trade only took shape after tea zones were declared in 1982, so this is a fairly modern kind of tea.

Today several gardens and small farm groups in Ilam and Dhankuta sell versions of it, among them Kanchanjangha's Kumari Gold and Shangri-La's Golden Tips. Sellers name second flush as the good season for it.
